primary_sources_read.sections_read: Published arbitrary-tiles source: Euclidean isometric copies, proved finite-d existence and final cardinality-bound conjecture. Source positive coordinate-permutation construction does not restrict the conjecture to such copies.
2021 punctured-interval theorem and retained cardinality-bound conjecture; arbitrary puncture is answered in dimension3.
2025 primary: one/two polygon isometry problems remain open; periodic means two translational symmetries. Three-polygon undecidability does not answer one connected square-grid polyomino.
2025 primary proves five-polyomino translation-only undecidability. Neither a single piece nor rotations/reflections target is resolved.

October8,2026 primary proves connected translational monotiling undecidable in3D, while2D translational monotiling is decidable. The target here is2D with rotations/reflections, not its already solved translation-only variant.
2018 primary proves bounded-remainder tiling when P has a minimum and maximum; Conjecture4 retains arbitrary finite P.

Primary abstract explicitly refutes general vertex-transitive power conjecture with odd non-prime-power tori, and refutes arbitrary hypercube edge-packing conjecture. Both historical source statements excluded.

Published geometric Hales–Jewett counterexample, maximal-line definition and concluding questions corresponding to thesis5.5–5.6. Counterexamples with no4-point line do not settle the strengthened questions.
Fixed-intersection definition, nonconstant maps versus bijections, sufficiently-large-n positive theorem and concluding questions. Same-source repeated conjecture merged.

Primary definitions and final Problems55–57: F-edges counted once when contained in an F-copy, rather than number of F-copies. Exact triangle theorem for large n and dense3-chromatic asymptotics are partial cases of the full classification.

accepted.title: Deciding square-grid tilings by one polyomino
accepted.text: A polyomino is a finite nonempty subset P⊂Z² connected by unit horizontal/vertical steps. A permitted copy is z+RP, with z∈Z² and R a signed permutation matrix, so rotations and reflections of the square grid are allowed. A tiling is a partition of Z² into such copies. Is there an algorithm that, given P, always halts and decides whether a tiling exists?

accepted.title: Bounded-remainder packing by an arbitrary finite poset
accepted.text: For every finite nonempty poset P, is there a constant c(P) such that for every n≥1 the Boolean lattice (2^[n],⊆) contains pairwise disjoint induced copies of P covering at least 2^n−c(P) elements? An induced copy is an injective map φ:P→2^[n] satisfying x≤_P y if and only if φ(x)⊆φ(y).

accepted.title: Forcing monochromatic lines from many long lines
accepted.text: For a finite point set S⊂R², a line means S∩ℓ for an affine line ℓ containing at least two points of S; all points of S on ℓ are included. Such a line is monochromatic if all its points have one colour. For every fixed k≥3 and l≥4, does some m=m(k,l) exist such that, whenever S determines at least m distinct lines each containing exactly l points and no line containing more than l points, every k-colouring of S has a monochromatic line?

accepted.title: Exact minima and extremizers for edges lying in F-copies
accepted.text: For every fixed finite simple graph F with an edge, every n≥1 and every integer 0≤e≤binom(n,2), determine the minimum, over n-vertex finite simple graphs G with exactly e edges, of the number of edges of G belonging to at least one subgraph isomorphic to F; characterize all graphs attaining the minimum. Count each such edge once, irrespective of the number of F-copies containing it, and do not require F-copies to be induced.
